startup.name: Amboras
startup.description: Amboras puts your entire e-commerce on autopilot. It builds your store, continuously optimizes it, reads your analytics, and learns what converts - all autonomously. No developers. No agencies. No guessing. Today it sells to humans. Tomorrow it sells to AI agents.

yc_acceptance.basis: Assumed accepted in this test, so this is a note. The published rate is about 1 percent of over 10,000 applicants per batch (references/yc_acceptance.md). An AI ecommerce autopilot from three founders fits YC's interest in AI agents, but the description shows no traction, merchants or founder credentials, and the space is crowded, so the starting rate gets no lift.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC could say no because Shopify, Wix and many AI website builders already offer store generation and optimization, the description has no merchants or revenue, and nothing indicates the team has ecommerce depth. The line about selling to AI agents later reads as a future story, not a present wedge.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2020-2023 --calibration-only: seed 60/72/77 cond 72% (n=103), series_a 19/22/35 cond 31% (n=74), series_b cond 26% (n=23), series_c cond 33% (n=6). Cross check --tag SaaS --years 2020-2023: seed cond 75%, A cond 31%, B cond 18% (n=11). Median months to seed for B2B 8 (p25 3, p75 22).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Slightly below the B2B anchor of 72% because the test needs a round above $500K within 12 months and the idea is crowded; held at 0.9 times anchor because AI products from YC batches in 2026 raise quickly and ecommerce tooling has precedent (Replo seed, Skio seed).

bands.rationale: A small SAFE round, common for a three person team before revenue.
Standard 2026 AI seed; market median about $3M on $18M pre money.
Upside if the product shows fast merchant revenue or a viral demo, as AI agent products have done in 2025 to 2026.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most likely miss is that investors see a thin wrapper on models and on Shopify style tools, ask for paying merchants, and find only free trials. Nextstore and Namaste Business, both YC ecommerce builders, never got past small notes, so a seed above $500K needs visible revenue the team may not have in 12 months.

ladder.why_it_fails: The Series A test is recurring revenue from merchants who stay and an edge Shopify cannot copy. Without that, investors will conclude Shopify Magic, Wix and generic AI builders erode the wedge, as incumbents copied Jemi and other store builder YC companies. Churn from small merchants is also high.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Ecommerce tooling YC companies in the data mostly end small: shutdowns such as Nextstore and Namaste Business, and acquisitions in the tens of millions such as Jemi and Preki. Reaching $100M or more needs a clear lead over Shopify's own AI tools, which the description does not show.

killers.risk: Shopify and website builders ship the same AI features
killers.evidence: Shopify, Wix and Squarespace already market AI store creation, and the YC analogs Jemi and Nextstore were hurt by incumbents.
killers.mitigation: Pick a niche vertical or an agent ready commerce layer that platforms are slow to build.

killers.risk: No proof that autonomous optimization beats humans
killers.evidence: Claims of continuous autonomous optimization need controlled lift data; merchants need tested results before giving up control.
killers.mitigation: Run A/B tests with launch merchants and publish lift numbers.

killers.risk: Small merchant churn and low price points
killers.evidence: Ecommerce builders sell to small merchants with high churn, and Skio grew only by moving mid sized merchants.
killers.mitigation: Focus on merchants with real traffic and bill on revenue share.

killers.risk: Selling to AI agents is a speculative future
killers.evidence: The description says tomorrow it sells to AI agents, but no standard exists yet for agent checkout.
killers.mitigation: Treat agent commerce as an option and keep human merchants as the revenue base.

competition_now.name: Shopify
competition_now.what: Dominant ecommerce platform with built in AI tools for store setup and content.

competition_now.name: Wix and Squarespace
competition_now.what: Website builders with AI site generation and store features.

competition_now.name: Replo and Shogun
competition_now.what: Page builders for Shopify focused on conversion.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating a store and reading analytics is feasible with current models in 3 months. The hard parts are reliable autonomy without breaking a live store, and proving conversion lift, both of which need real merchant data.

takeover_risk.rationale: Shopify and AI builders can ship similar features within months and already own merchants. Platform dependence is the central risk and 5 of 5 is justified.

evidence.claim: Merchants pay for page builders and optimization apps, shown by Replo and Shogun, which have large customer counts.
Shopify markets AI store creation, evidence that the platform sees the need.

actions: Onboard 10 live stores and measure conversion lift.
Publish a before and after case.
roadmap.proof: At least 10 paying merchants and a measured lift.

actions: Pick one merchant segment and sell directly.
roadmap.proof: Monthly recurring revenue and churn under 5%.

pros.point: Clear value claim and a precedent that ecommerce tools can raise seeds.
pros.evidence: Replo raised a $4.2M seed and Skio reached about $32M ARR per the YC data.

pros.point: AI agent products are being funded quickly in 2026.
pros.evidence: The YC data shows multiple 2025 AI agent companies raising seeds within months of their batch.

brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Amboras" --era 2022+ returned invented_or_proper, 1 word, 3 syllables.
weaknesses: Easy to confuse with other A names
brand.rationale: An invented word like many YC names. It does not describe the product, so the one liner AI Native Shopify does the explaining, as with other invented word brands such as Replo.

narrative.headline: A crowded AI ecommerce wedge: plausible for a seed, but platform copy risk caps later rounds.
narrative.general_summary: Amboras bets on AI doing the job of a store builder and optimizer. Ecommerce tools have raised seeds before, such as Replo and Skio, so the seed step looks reachable. The main risk is that Shopify and AI builders offer the same features. Later rounds depend on revenue and retention that the description does not show. It is a forecast from the input file and the base rates only, with no knowledge of what happened after the batch started, and the numbers should be read with wide error bars because the cohorts for these categories are small.

assumptions: Seed means a round above $500K within 12 months of 2026-04-06.
Only the input file was used for the company; market claims were not re-verified.
